newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Once-shunned Philippine food stocks gain favour.
newsitem.headline: Once-shunned Philippine food stocks gain favour.

text.p: Philippine food and beverage companies, after lagging the stock market for more than a year, are once again flavour of the month, analysts said on Monday.
Food stocks were being buoyed by a recovery in the agricultural sector and the traditionally heavy consumer spending of the Christmas season, analysts said.
"Risks in the consumer sector have been overplayed and now the sector is beginning to outperform the market," said Tina Ibarra, an analyst of Socgen-Crosby UBP Securities Inc.
The brokerage house said the food and beverage sector was set for 30 percent growth in earnings per share (EPS) in 1997 compared with the flat 3.2 percent estimated for 1996.
Two weeks ago, the sector was trading at 13 times forecast 1997 earnings. It is now at 15 times, a par with the market, according to the brokerage house.
Analysts said San Miguel Corp, Alaska Milk Corp and Cosmos Bottling Corp were the market's favourites.
Food and beverage companies comprise about 10 percent of the composite index, with San Miguel alone accounting for nine percent.

Food stocks have been battered since last year by high prices for milk, sugar, corn and wheat, which were driven up by a prolonged drought and a series of typhoons that ravaged the Philippines in 1994 and 1995.
But better weather has helped farm-sector stocks rally by 4.17 percent in the first three quarters of this year.
"The market is looking at the food sector as a recovery play," said Raul Ruiz, vice president of Sun Hung Kai Securities.
"But we're buying it for the long term. It's the beginning of a three-year consumer boom to commence in 1997," said Jose Salceda, director of SBC Warburg.
The food and beverage sector absorbs about 55 percent of personal consumption expenditures, which in turn account for 74 percent of gross national product (GNP) in the Philippines.

Salceda said per capita GNP had grown well ahead of expectations, reaching $1,100 at the end of 1995. He expects per capita GNP to reach $1,650 in line with forecasts of seven to eight percent annual GNP growth in the next few years, fueling further growth in the food sector.
Sun Hung Kai's Ruiz, however, cautioned investors against being too bullish on food stocks, warning that inflation could heat up next year due to recent demands for higher wages.
Inflation averaged 9.1 percent from January to October compared with 9.7 percent for the same period in 1995.
"The recovery of the whole sector is still fragile. It could be derailed," Ruiz said.
Socgen-Crosby UBP Securities forecast San Miguel's EPS to grow by 18 percent to 2.71 in 1997 from a 1996 estimate of 2.30 pesos.
Its Class A shares closed the Monday morning session at 47.0 pesos, while its B shares ended at 98.50.
SBC Warburg predicted Alaska Milk's EPS would double to 0.26 peso in 1997 from the 0.13 peso forecast for 1996. Alaska Milk closed on Monday morning at 3.05 pesos.
Cosmos Bottling's EPS in 1997 is seen at 0.41 peso, up 32 percent from the 0.31 peso estimate for 1996, Sun Hung Kai said. Cosmos was at 6.90 pesos after the morning session.
